files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close checklist

Owner: N. Vartanian. Complete in sequence and leave support for each step.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 that pays in July; some months have every run paid in-month. If such a period exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule, contracts, and the GL. If it is not already posted, book June prepaid amortization as ONE combined journal entry—do not duplicate an existing entry. Take a full month of amortization in the month an item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after checking the GL to confirm it has not already been recorded.
5. Verify the expense coding on June vendor bills by comparing the bill documents with the GL, and reclass anything miscoded.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, after all work in items 1-5 has been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Foxhall Consulting Group began in 2018 when a small circle of former operations leads started helping local companies untangle projects that had stalled between planning and execution. What began as informal working sessions grew into a practical advisory firm serving organizations that needed experienced hands without adding permanent management layers.

The firm sells project-based consulting, operating-model reviews, process improvement, implementation support, and focused management workshops. Its clients tend to value plain language, tidy workplans, and recommendations that can actually be used after the consultants leave. Engagements range from short diagnostic assignments to longer efforts involving several client teams.

The Foxhall team has a low-ego, roll-up-your-sleeves character. Senior consultants stay close to delivery, while coordinators keep meetings, research, and client materials moving. The office culture favors marked-up drafts, quick morning check-ins, and candid conversations over elaborate presentations. Team members bring backgrounds in logistics, analytics, professional services, and general business operations.

Today, the company is an ordinary going concern with an established client base and a steady mix of advisory and implementation work. Leadership is concentrating on consistent delivery, clearer service packages, stronger referral relationships, and better internal documentation as the practice matures.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Keep the Foxhall Consulting Group voice practical, senior-led, and free of management jargon. The aim is to make the firm easier to recognize and easier to refer.

## Priorities

- Refresh core messaging and visual templates so proposals, case studies, and event materials feel like one brand.
- Publish short field notes built around recurring client problems: stalled implementations, unclear ownership, and overloaded operating teams.
- Run two useful, discussion-led webinars per quarter, with follow-up summaries for attendees and prospects.
- Test a partner co-marketing pilot with a complementary services firm. Favor a joint briefing or workshop over a generic promotional campaign.
- Build a lightweight referral kit for former clients and professional contacts.
- Improve consultant bios and service pages with clearer examples of how engagements work.

## Rhythm by quarter

### Q3

Finalize messaging, update the standard content library, launch the first webinar sequence, and identify the pilot partner.

### Q4

Deliver the partner activity, continue the webinar cadence, publish client-safe case examples, and review which channels produced credible conversations.

## Measures

Track qualified introductions, webinar participation, follow-up meetings, partner-sourced opportunities, content reuse, and feedback from active clients. Keep reporting simple enough that the team will maintain it.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Notes from your predecessor

N. Vartanian — a few things worth knowing before you finish the close:

- The bank usually posts its own fees and service charges near the end of the statement. We have historically booked those at close rather than during the month, so check the final statement activity carefully.
- Please do not trust the first-pass coding on every June vendor bill. A couple may be sitting in the wrong expense account. The documents in `bills/` are authoritative; use them as the source of truth and reclass the GL where needed.
- The Q2 budget was locked in early April. One-off items that arrived in June were never included, and they are the main reason some variances will look unusually large.
- Payroll timing is not fixed. Do not assume the second monthly run pays in July: its pay date varies, so verify the actual timing in the payroll register.
